real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage rates climbed again, to 7.37%, as the 10-Year closed at its highest since 2007.
real_estate.commentary:
Rates climbed for a second straight day. Mortgage News Daily has the 30-year at 7.37% as of today, up 0.11, and the 15-year at 7.00%, up 0.13. Both are new 52 week highs, topping yesterday's. The newsletter printed 7.26% and 6.87%, which were Wednesday's readings.

The bond market is the reason (chart above). The 10-Year closed Wednesday at 5.11%, up 0.15 in a single session and its highest close since July 2007. It has climbed 114 basis points from February's 3.97% low, and it was at 5.16% at 11:49 AM PT today, so the pressure has not let up.

Here is what that means on a real Fremont home. At today's median on market list price of $1,238,944, with 20% down, the loan is $991,155, which is still high balance conforming here, not jumbo. Principal and interest is $6,842 a month at 7.37%, against $5,936 at 5.99%, the 52 week low. That is $906 more every month for the same house.

• Board wide: 2,740 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 192 coming soon and 179 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 707 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 615 are on the market and 92 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 256 live, 204 active, 40 coming soon, 12 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,238,944 at $798 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 29 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 184, Milpitas 114, Newark 86, Union City 67.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,098,000 at $680 a square foot. 278 homes are priced under a million, and 166 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

What this means for you: supply edged up to 707 from 705 and the pile of homes past 60 days shrank to 166 from 171, so listings are still moving even as rates rise. Buyers: get a written quote this week and compare the 30-year FHA at 6.98% and a 7/6 ARM at 6.80% against the 7.37% fixed, because the gap now buys real payment room. Sellers: the same house now costs a buyer about $900 more a month than it did at the 52 week low, so price to this week's rate, not to spring's.

stocks.note: Levels are Wednesday, September 23 at the closing bell. Thursday is live and roughly flat: at 11:49 AM PT the S&P was 7,705.96 (0.00%), the Dow 51,361.56 (-0.29%) and the Nasdaq 26,933.52 (-0.01%).
stocks.news: Wednesday was a rate day. The jump in the 10-Year pulled all three indexes lower, with the Nasdaq down 1.13% and the S&P off 0.75%. McDonald's fell 4.81% after saying the fast food slowdown is sticking, with U.S. sales at existing stores up just 0.8% last quarter and beef costs a big part of the squeeze. Thursday is holding steady so far.

economy.note: All four are Wednesday, September 23. The 10-Year is the Treasury daily yield curve close, gold and silver are the COMEX front month settlement against Tuesday's settlement, and Brent is the ICE front month (November contract) settlement.
economy.commentary:
Beef is the chart today. The Bureau of Labor Statistics has 100% ground beef at a record $6.92 a pound this August, up 55% from $4.47 in August 2021. In the West, the closest region BLS publishes to us, it is $7.44, up 53%. The newsletter said beef prices have roughly doubled in five years; the government's own numbers say closer to half again. The version of this chart going around showed $6.88, which was July; August set the record.

The 10-Year closed at 5.11%, up 0.15 on the day and the highest since July 2007. The newsletter printed 5.12% and called it up 0.01; the Treasury curve says 5.11% and up 0.15. It credits strong economic data, a weakly received government bond sale and Fed talk of more hikes.

Gold settled down 1.33% at $4,318.40 and silver down 2.35% at $64.96 as yields rose. Brent went the other way, settling at $103.08, up 3.86%. The newsletter printed Brent at $91.85; the front month settlement is $103.08, a gap too large to be rounding, so we go with the exchange.

feature_image.alt: Paired bar chart of the average retail price per pound of 100% ground beef every August from 2021 to 2026. U.S. city average: $4.47, $4.94, $5.08, $5.58, $6.32, $6.92. West region: $4.87, $5.56, $5.81, $6.46, $6.84, $7.44.
feature_image.caption: Ground beef hit a record $6.92 a pound nationally this August, up 55% in five years. The West, the closest region BLS publishes to the Bay Area, is at $7.44.
feature_image.source: Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics average price data, series APU0000703112 and APU0400703112, August of each year.

crypto.commentary:
Crypto is catching its breath after Wednesday's drop. Bitcoin is at $84,377, up 0.13% over 24 hours, Ether is up 0.84% to $2,687 and XRP leads at $1.53, up 2.52%. Prices are live from CoinGecko at 11:49 AM PT.

It is a quiet bounce, not a reversal. Bitcoin is still about $2,000 below where it closed Monday, before the jump in yields sent the riskiest assets lower.
